title: This Is Why We Lift
summary: A compilation of 'things I wish I knew before lifting' segments from natural creators (GVS, Stand Strength, AlphaDestiny, Bald Omni Man, Basement Bodybuilding, Fazlifts, Tom Lazorik, FreakieD) interleaved with NH's own segments. NH's parts stress that programs must adapt, there is no final program or finish line, the need for a program as a map, keeping your own goals, avoiding stubbornness, and not setting deadlines.
claims: A program works for you, not the reverse; it is a piece of paper you wrote and you can modify any line
Two years earlier he dogmatically pushed the idea of a final program; there is no such thing because your body evolves forever
Forever stupidity: every five years you should look back and see you were an idiot; if not, you stopped progressing
There is no finish line in lifting and no fixed natural limit; you must keep adapting to keep moving forward
If you do not have a goal, others (influencers) will hand you one that serves them; set your own goal and program
If you want to be happy, be happy now; deferring happiness until a goal is reached leaves you just as miserable
The first important thing as a man is to build your identity, otherwise you cannot know what will fulfill you
Being stubborn with one method that has proven not to work is like backing up to run harder into a wall
A method that works now might not work in a month; keep an eye open for innovation and do not box yourself in
Stuck in a powerlifting mindset, it took him roughly from 2017-18 to 2020-21 just to transition to proper bodybuilding training
Not having a map gets you lost; once on the wrong path you have to walk all the way back before reaching the right one
For his first two years he trained without a program; he still gained, but a plan would have been far more productive
Early on it is useful not to be too optimal: try new things and make mistakes to develop instinct
A program is a map or architectural plan to your goal physique; lifting without one is just moving your body around
Most of what you consume on YouTube should be information; 70% entertainment / 30% information is wasting your life and making others money
Good teachers admit they used to be stupid; advanced lifters all started small and have simply been at it longer
Having a goal physique is good because it dictates a program, but never put a deadline on it; deadlines make you rush and take shortcuts
When he got started he was patient and enjoyed the journey; chasing the finish line turned lifting into a punishment he inflicted on himself
Fitness content promising results in weeks plays on your fears, insecurities and impatience
The natural community should pool experience and pass knowledge to the younger generation without expecting anything in return
(Guest GVS) Boring workouts build more muscle than epic ones; Instagram workouts are useless because novelty drives clicks
(Guest Stand Strength) Do not learn more than you can apply; pick something, stick with it, change one thing at a time
(Guest Basement Bodybuilding) Optimal on paper is useless if you do not enjoy it; but only doing what you are good at leaves weaknesses
(Guest Bald Omni Man) Do not talk during sets: habitual chatting lowers your long-term training intensity to that of a sedentary snail
(Guest Stand Strength) Steroids are injecting time into your muscles; the main differentiator between lifters is training age
(Guest Bald Omni Man) Pushing through pain equals ER, pushing through discomfort equals PR; listen to warning signs like weeks of elbow pain
(Guest AlphaDestiny) Elite naturals all got big through different methods, so everything works and the best approach is the one you can stick to
(Guest Basement Bodybuilding) Record progress with photos in consistent lighting, measurements and body weight, not just strength; his arms went from 15.75 to over 16.5 inches cold
(Guest Tom Lazorik) Diets must be sustainable; he lost over 100 lb but never learned maintenance
(Guest) Calories in vs out drives weight change; the anabolic window and eating every 2-3 hours are myths
(Guest Fazlifts) Learn to cook and if overfat, lose the fat first before chasing size
(Guest Stand Strength) Supplements are mostly useless; tiredness needs sleep, low protein needs food
(Guest Bald Omni Man) Gigabulking on 5000 kcal of junk makes you feel sluggish and is unnecessary
(Guest Fazlifts) Patience and a plan let him go from a 90 kg bench he was told was his genetic limit to 180 kg
(Guest Bald Omni Man) Powerlifting-only training with no isolation is hogwash; work every muscle group
